raw_responses.Bulgarian:
The figure is a bar chart illustrating the relationship between Sparsity Rate and Perplexity, with a distinction between "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" metrics. The horizontal axis represents Sparsity Rate, with categories labeled as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, presented in ascending order. The vertical axis represents Perplexity, using a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³. The scale is labeled with powers of 10 (10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³). Two sets of bars are presented for each Sparsity Rate: one in blue representing "Per-Output" and one in orange representing "Per-Layer". For the 10% and 20% sparsity rates, both "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" bars are very short and have similar heights. As the Sparsity Rate increases, both "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" values generally increase, with the "Per-Layer" values consistently higher than the "Per-Output" values. At 80% Sparsity Rate, the "Per-Output" bar reaches a height corresponding to approximately 8x10², while the "Per-Layer" bar reaches a height corresponding to approximately 1x10³.
